tour.title: Project Orientation
tour.description: Start with the Vite HTML shell and package manifest to see how the learning workspace is delivered and which development commands drive it. The application is a private React package with data generation, type-checking, build, and Vitest test workflows. This gives the surrounding context for the code explored next.

tour.title: React Bootstrap
tour.description: The browser entry point mounts the React tree in Strict Mode and loads the global stylesheet. Its root component then wires together shared learning state, the application shell, and hash-routed page views. Read these files together for the top-level runtime flow.
tour.languageLesson: React applications commonly bootstrap once with createRoot, then compose providers and routes beneath a root component; Strict Mode helps surface unsafe development-time behavior.

tour.title: Shared Application Shell
tour.description: The shell supplies the persistent header, primary navigation, and main-content landmark that frame every route. Global CSS establishes the shared visual foundation around those reusable layout pieces. This separation keeps page components focused on their individual learning workflows.

tour.title: Repository Learning Data
tour.description: The generated repository snapshot and its type definitions provide the static learning material consumed throughout the interface. Understanding this contract first makes it easier to follow how pages display topics, notes, and problem metadata. The relationship map adds the explicit topic-to-concept links used by the knowledge view.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript types act as shared contracts: they describe the generated data shape without adding runtime code, so producers and React consumers can be checked together.

tour.title: Personal Learning State
tour.description: Personal type definitions establish the vocabulary for tasks and solve sessions, while storage loads and saves that data in the browser. The learning-state module builds on those foundations with a reducer, provider, and hooks for shared UI access. This is the stateful core behind the workspace’s personal progress features.
tour.languageLesson: A React context provider paired with reducer-driven state centralizes updates while custom hooks give components a focused read or dispatch interface.

tour.title: Today Task Workflow
tour.description: The Today page brings repository data and personal state together into the daily learning flow. Its composer and list components isolate task input and task rendering, keeping the page responsible for coordination. Follow these components after the state layer to see how user actions become persisted progress.

tour.title: Practice Recommendations
tour.description: Recommendation helpers select and filter practice work, count weekly completions, and provide the daily suggestion logic. The LeetCode page consumes those functions along with shared learning state to turn the repository index into an interactive practice view. This keeps selection rules independent from presentation.
tour.languageLesson: Separating pure selection functions from React components makes recommendation behavior easier to test and reuse without rendering a UI.

tour.title: Knowledge Map View
tour.description: The knowledge-map page combines active topics, repository statistics, notes, and the relationship data introduced earlier. It gives learners a connected view of the material rather than treating each repository item in isolation. This is the main visualization-oriented endpoint of the static data layer.

tour.title: Data Generation Tooling
tour.description: The generation script turns repository learning material into the browser-safe TypeScript module consumed by the frontend. Its repository-data helper collects notes, topics, languages, and problem indexes, while fixtures exercise valid and duplicate-content cases. Study this path to understand how source content becomes UI data at build time.

tour.title: Verification and Toolchain
tour.description: The test setup and representative component, domain, state, and tooling tests verify the main learning workflows and data-processing behavior. Vite configuration connects the frontend toolchain to the test environment, while TypeScript configuration enforces strict application checks. Finish here to see the safety net around the application and its generator.
